title: Test Project 7
description: launched a community-led clean water project to address declining water quality in local streams and wells caused by soil erosion, agricultural runoff, and inadequate sanitation infrastructure. For years, families relied on untreated surface water for household use, increasing health risks and limiting productivity. Recognizing the connection between environmental stewardship and community well-being, farmers came together to design a sustainable solution that would protect their shared water sources while strengthening agricultural resilience. The project focused on restoring watershed health and improving access to safe drinking water. Farmers established vegetative buffer zones along riverbanks to reduce runoff, planted native trees to stabilize soil, and adopted soil conservation practices such as cover cropping and reduced tillage. In parallel, the community installed a gravity-fed water filtration system and constructed protected spring catchments to ensure clean, reliable water
